# Moving Day Essentials — One-Page Checklist

*Print this and keep it in the car.*

---

**DOCUMENTS POUCH (keep on person or front seat)**
☐ Driver's licenses, passports, SS cards
☐ Vehicle titles, registrations, insurance cards
☐ Lease/closing papers (both homes)
☐ Moving contract + Bill of Lading + inventory
☐ Vet records, rabies cert, microchip #, meds list
☐ Medical records + prescriptions
☐ Bank/card contact numbers
☐ Cash ($200–$400) + checkbook

**TECH BAG**
☐ Phones + chargers (car + wall)
☐ Laptop + charger
☐ Portable battery pack
☐ Headphones
☐ USB drive with photo backups
☐ Paper map / atlas (backup)

**OVERNIGHT BAG (per person)**
☐ 3 days of clothes + pajamas
☐ Toiletries, meds, glasses/contacts
☐ Towel, phone charger
☐ Comfortable driving shoes

**DOG KIT**
☐ Leash, collar with updated tag, harness
☐ Crate or car barrier
☐ Food (5+ days) + bowls + treats
☐ Water + collapsible bowl
☐ Poop bags, wipes, paper towels
☐ Bed/blanket + favorite toy
☐ Meds + calming aid
☐ Vet records (paper copy)
☐ Recent photo (in case lost)

**CAR EMERGENCY KIT**
☐ Jumper cables, tire gauge, spare tire check
☐ First aid kit
☐ Flashlight + batteries
☐ Blanket, work gloves
☐ Water (1 gal) + snacks/protein bars
☐ Reflective triangles or flares
☐ Multi-tool, duct tape, zip ties

**FIRST-NIGHT BOX (opens first at new home)**
☐ Toilet paper, hand soap, paper towels
☐ Shower curtain + towels
☐ Sheets + pillows for one bed
☐ Trash bags
☐ Basic tools (screwdriver, hammer, box cutter)
☐ Phone chargers
☐ Coffee/tea + mugs + kettle or French press
☐ Plates, forks, 1 pan, dish soap, sponge
☐ Dog food + bowls + bed

**LAST-MINUTE WALK-THROUGH (Ohio)**
☐ All rooms, closets, cabinets empty
☐ Fridge/freezer empty, cleaned, propped open
☐ Windows locked, lights off
☐ Thermostat set
☐ Final meter read photo
☐ Keys/remotes returned, receipt obtained
☐ Walk-through photos/video taken

**ON ARRIVAL (Oregon)**
☐ Photo/video of new place before unloading
☐ Note any damage in writing to landlord
☐ Confirm utilities on (power, water, gas, internet)
☐ Locate breaker box, water shutoff, gas shutoff
☐ Dog on leash until yard is secure

---

# 6-Week Calendar Reminders (Copy/Paste Ready)

Format: **Days before Move Day = Day 0.** Set each as an event or reminder in Google/Apple Calendar. Replace "MOVE DAY" with your actual date.

## Week 6 (Days -42 to -36)

**Day -42, 9:00 AM — Confirm mover/truck booking + deposit paid**
Verify USDOT #, insurance, deposit receipt saved.

**Day -42, 7:00 PM — Start declutter: garage + storage**
2 hrs. Sort keep/sell/donate/trash.

**Day -40, 10:00 AM — Schedule Oregon internet install**
Book earliest available date post-arrival.

**Day -38, 6:00 PM — Research Oregon DMV + emissions requirements**
Know which county you'll register in.

**Day -36, 9:00 AM — Book temporary housing (if needed) + lodging on route**
Dog-friendly only. Confirm pet fees.

## Week 5 (Days -35 to -29)

**Day -35, 9:00 AM — Send written notice to landlord / finalize sale timeline**

**Day -33, 6:00 PM — Vet visit: records, rabies cert, meds refill**

**Day -31, 7:00 PM — Declutter: closets + guest room** (2 hrs)

**Day -30, 10:00 AM — Order packing supplies**
Boxes, tape, wrap, markers, labels.

**Day -29, 9:00 AM — Notify employer of move date + confirm remote/relocation terms**

## Week 4 (Days -28 to -22)

**Day -28, 9:00 AM — Book vehicle shipping OR finalize drive route**

**Day -26, 7:00 PM — Begin packing: non-essential rooms** (2 hrs)

**Day -24, 10:00 AM — Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs (day after move)**

**Day -24, 10:30 AM — Schedule Oregon utility start dates (arrival day)**

**Day -22, 6:00 PM — Car maintenance appointment**
Oil, tires, brakes, fluids, battery.

## Week 3 (Days -21 to -15)

**Day -21, 9:00 AM — Confirm mover arrival window + crew + payment method**

**Day -20, 9:00 AM — Call auto insurer: Oregon coverage transition**

**Day -19, 7:00 PM — Pack: kitchen non-essentials + decor** (2 hrs)

**Day -17, 10:00 AM — Schedule donation pickup / post sale items**

**Day -15, 9:00 AM — Confirm first Oregon vet appointment booked**

## Week 2 (Days -14 to -8)

**Day -14, 9:00 AM — Submit USPS change of address** (effective move day)

**Day -14, 9:30 AM — Update address: banks, cards, SSA, insurers, subscriptions**

**Day -13, 7:00 PM — Pack: bedrooms + bathrooms non-essentials** (2 hrs)

**Day -12, 10:00 AM — Order new dog ID tag with new address/phone**

**Day -11, 6:00 PM — Photograph valuables + record serial numbers**

**Day -10, 9:00 AM — Confirm vehicle shipping pickup OR finalize lodging bookings**

**Day -9, 7:00 PM — Pack: living room + remaining rooms** (2 hrs)

**Day -8, 9:00 AM — Set aside Documents Pouch items in one folder**

## Week 1 (Days -7 to -1)

**Day -7, 9:00 AM — Final confirmation call: mover, utilities, internet install**

**Day -6, 10:00 AM — Withdraw cash for moving day ($200–$400)**

**Day -5, 7:00 PM — Pack First-Night Box + label clearly**

**Day -4, 9:00 AM — Confirm dog travel kit packed + meds on hand**

**Day -3, 10:00 AM — Defrost + clean fridge/freezer; donate perishables**

**Day -2, 9:00 AM — Fill car with gas; pack car emergency kit + overnight bags**

**Day -1, 10:00 AM — Final walk-through prep: photos, meter read plan, key return**

**Day -1, 8:00 PM — Charge all devices + power banks; set early alarm**

## Move Day & After

**Day 0, 6:00 AM — MOVE DAY: Walk-through photos → load → meter read → keys returned**

**Day 0, 7:00 AM — Dog secured in crate/safe room during loading**

**Day +1 to +3 — Drive days: break every 2–3 hrs for dog, log mileage/fuel**

**Day +4, 10:00 AM — Arrival walk-through photos + damage notes to landlord**

**Day +4, 2:00 PM — Test utilities; locate shutoffs + breaker box**

**Day +5, 9:00 AM — Renter's insurance active (if not already)**

**Day +7, 9:00 AM — Oregon DMV: driver's license appointment**

**Day +8, 10:00 AM — Oregon DMV: vehicle registration + emissions (if required)**

**Day +9, 9:00 AM — First Oregon vet visit + update microchip registry**

**Day +10, 10:00 AM — Apply for county/city dog license**

**Day +14, 9:00 AM — Cancel Ohio registration/plates; confirm all Ohio utilities closed**

---

**Tip for calendar sync:** In Google Calendar, create a dedicated "Move" calendar (so you can hide it later). In Apple Calendar, make a new list called "Move." Paste each reminder as a separate event — the title is the bolded line, the description is the line below it.

# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

**Packing order principle:** Pack from least-used to most-used. Storage and decor first, kitchen and bathrooms last. Target 1 room per packing session (2–3 hrs). Start 4 weeks out, finish the day before the move.

---

## LABELING SYSTEM

Use this on every box. Takes 15 seconds, saves hours on arrival.

**Top line:** Room (e.g., KITCHEN)
**Second line:** Contents summary (e.g., "Pots, pans, baking sheets")
**Third line:** Priority code:
- **A** = First-night box, open immediately
- **B** = Open within 3 days
- **C** = Open within 2 weeks
- **D** = Storage, open when needed

**Side marks:**
- Red dot or "FRAGILE" on 2 sides + top
- Arrow + "THIS SIDE UP" if contents require it
- Number boxes per room (e.g., "KITCHEN 3 of 12") — helps spot missing boxes

**Color-code with tape or markers** (optional but fast at destination):
- Blue = Kitchen
- Green = Bedroom
- Yellow = Living room
- Red = Bathroom
- Black = Office
- Orange = Garage/storage

**Keep a master inventory** in a shared Google Sheet: box #, room, contents, priority, who packed it.

---

## BOX TYPES — WHAT TO BUY

| Box Type | Use For | Approx. Qty for 1–2 BR |
|---|---|---|
| Small (1.5 cu ft) | Books, canned goods, tools, heavy items | 15–20 |
| Medium (3.0 cu ft) | Kitchenware, decor, toys, small appliances | 25–35 |
| Large (4.5 cu ft) | Linens, pillows, lampshades, light bulky items | 10–15 |
| Extra-large (6.0 cu ft) | Comforters, large pillows, lightweight bulk only | 3–5 |
| Dish pack (double-walled) | Dishes, glassware, ceramics | 3–5 |
| Wardrobe box | Hanging clothes, long coats | 2–4 |
| Mirror/picture box | Framed art, mirrors, TVs | 3–6 |
| Mattress bag | Each mattress | 1 per bed |

**Supplies to buy:**
Packing tape (6–8 rolls), bubble wrap (1 large roll), packing paper (1 bundle = ~10 lbs), stretch wrap, box cutters (2), permanent markers (4–5), ziplock bags (assorted), colored tape or labels, furniture blankets (rent from mover or buy cheap).

**Free box sources:** liquor stores (strongest), grocery stores, bookstores, neighborhood Buy Nothing groups, Facebook Marketplace.

---

## FRAGILE HANDLING RULES

- Never pack fragile items with empty space — fill gaps with paper or clothing.
- Heavy items on bottom, light on top, within every box.
- Dishes stand vertically (like records), never stacked flat.
- Wrap each glass item individually before boxing.
- Use original boxes for electronics if you kept them.
- TVs: use a TV box with foam corners; always transport upright.
- Mirrors and art: tape an X across the glass to contain shatter, wrap in paper, then bubble wrap, then box.
- Lamps: remove bulbs and shades, wrap shades separately in large boxes.
- Mark every fragile box on top + 2 sides.
- Weight limit: no box over 50 lbs. Small boxes for heavy stuff, large for light.

---

## DECLUTTER PRINCIPLES (apply in every room)

- **The 12-month rule:** Haven't used it in a year? Donate or sell.
- **Cost-to-move test:** If replacing it costs less than moving it, don't move it.
- **One-in, one-out during packing:** For every "keep" pile, pull one item to donate.
- **4-box method per room:** Keep / Donate / Sell / Trash. Label actual boxes, don't just mentally sort.
- **Sell timeline:** List items 4+ weeks out. After 2 weeks unsold, donate. Don't let unsold items derail the move.
- **Donation options:** Goodwill, Salvation Army, Habitat ReStore (furniture), local shelters (towels/blankets), Buy Nothing groups, Freecycle.
- **Hazardous items you can't move:** Movers won't take paint, propane, gasoline, fireworks, ammunition, cleaning chemicals, aerosols, nail polish. Use them up, give them away, or dispose at a hazardous waste facility.

---

## ROOM-BY-ROOM

### Week 4 (Days -28 to -22): Low-use spaces first

---

**GARAGE / BASEMENT / STORAGE** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 4–6 hrs** (split over 2 sessions)

*Pack first because it's the hardest and most cluttered.*

- [ ] Declutter: tools, old paint, sports gear, holiday decor
- [ ] Dispose of hazardous items properly (paint, chemicals, propane)
- [ ] Drain gas from lawnmower/weed trimmer or sell them
- [ ] Pack tools in small boxes (heavy)
- [ ] Pack holiday decor in medium boxes, label by holiday
- [ ] Pack sports/outdoor gear in large boxes
- [ ] Wrap bikes in stretch wrap; remove pedals if tight on space
- [ ] Label: **GARAGE — [contents] — D**

**Boxes needed:** 5 small, 6 medium, 3 large
**Declutter tip:** Garages hide the most "I'll use it someday" items. Be ruthless. If it's rusted, broken, or duplicate — out.

---

**ATTIC / SEASONAL STORAGE** — **Responsible: P** — **Time: 2–3 hrs**

- [ ] Sort seasonal clothing: keep current + next season accessible
- [ ] Pack off-season clothes in large boxes or vacuum bags
- [ ] Decor (seasonal, sentimental): medium boxes, wrap breakables
- [ ] Old paperwork: shred what you don't need; scan what you do
- [ ] Label: **STORAGE — [contents] — D**

**Boxes needed:** 4 medium, 3 large
**Declutter tip:** If you didn't unpack it from the last move, you probably don't need it.

---

**GUEST ROOM / SPARE ROOM** — **Responsible: M** — **Time: 2 hrs**

- [ ] Strip bed; wash and pack linens in large boxes
- [ ] Pack decor and wall art in mirror boxes
- [ ] Clear closet: donate anything not worn in 12 months
- [ ] Pack remaining clothes in wardrobe box or vacuum bags
- [ ] Disassemble bed frame last week; bag hardware + tape to frame
- [ ] Label: **GUEST ROOM — [contents] — C**

**Boxes needed:** 2 medium, 2 large, 1 mirror box

---

### Week 3 (Days -21 to -15): Semi-used spaces

---

**HOME OFFICE** — **Responsible: P** — **Time: 3–4 hrs**

- [ ] Back up computer to cloud + external drive **before** packing
- [ ] Photograph cable setups before unplugging (saves hours later)
- [ ] Bag cables with labels (laptop charger, monitor, etc.)
- [ ] Shred old documents; scan important ones
- [ ] Pack books in **small** boxes only (they get heavy fast)
- [ ] Pack monitor in original box if possible, otherwise mirror box
- [ ] Office supplies in medium box
- [ ] Keep current work items + laptop out until Day -2
- [ ] Label: **OFFICE — [contents] — B**

**Boxes needed:** 4 small, 3 medium, 1 mirror box
**Fragile:** Monitor, printer — wrap in bubble wrap, box with paper fill
**Declutter tip:** Toss outdated manuals, warranties for items you no longer own, dead pens, cables for devices you don't have.

---

**DINING ROOM** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 2 hrs**

- [ ] Wrap and pack china, serveware in dish packs (vertical)
- [ ] Table linens in medium box
- [ ] Decor, candles, centerpieces: wrap fragile items
- [ ] Disassemble table (week of move); bag hardware
- [ ] Wrap chairs in furniture blankets or stretch wrap
- [ ] Label: **DINING — [contents] — C** (A if daily-use dishes)

**Boxes needed:** 2 dish packs, 2 medium
**Fragile:** All china and glassware — individual wrap, vertical pack, "FRAGILE" on 3 sides

---

**LIVING ROOM** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 3 hrs**

- [ ] Photograph TV cables before unplugging
- [ ] Pack books in small boxes
- [ ] Decor, vases, picture frames in medium boxes with heavy wrap
- [ ] Wall art and mirrors in mirror boxes (X-tape glass first)
- [ ] TV in TV box, transport upright
- [ ] Lampshades wrapped and packed separately in large boxes; bulbs removed
- [ ] Rugs rolled and wrapped in stretch wrap
- [ ] Remote controls, cables bagged and labeled
- [ ] Couch cushions in large bags; wrap couch in moving blankets week-of
- [ ] Label: **LIVING ROOM — [contents] — B**

**Boxes needed:** 4 small, 4 medium, 2 large, 2–4 mirror boxes, 1 TV box
**Fragile:** TV, mirrors, art, lamps — all require corner protection

---

### Week 2 (Days -14 to -8): Everyday spaces, first pass

---

**PRIMARY BEDROOM** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 3–4 hrs across 2 sessions**

*Session 1 (Day -14):* Non-essentials
- [ ] Off-season clothes: wardrobe boxes or vacuum bags
- [ ] Shoes you're not wearing this month: medium boxes
- [ ] Jewelry: keep with you in a small zippered pouch (not in truck)
- [ ] Books, decor, photos: small/medium boxes
- [ ] Wall art: mirror boxes

*Session 2 (Day -3):* Remaining
- [ ] Remaining clothes in wardrobe boxes
- [ ] Bedding except what you're sleeping in — pack 2 sets in A-priority box
- [ ] Nightstand contents
- [ ] Disassemble bed frame Day -1; bag + tape hardware to frame
- [ ] Mattress in mattress bag

**Boxes needed:** 3 wardrobe, 3 medium, 2 large, 1 mirror box, 1 mattress bag
**Declutter tip:** Clothes you haven't worn in a year, mismatched socks, worn-out shoes, expired cosmetics — all go.
**Keep aside:** Jewelry, important documents, meds, 3 days of clothes in overnight bag

---

**BATHROOMS** — **Responsible: M** — **Time: 1–2 hrs per bathroom**

*Guest bath (Day -10):*
- [ ] Toss expired me

turns.text:
# Room-by-Room Packing (Continued)

---

**BATHROOMS** — **Responsible: M** — **Time: 1–2 hrs per bathroom**

*Guest bath (Day -10):*
- [ ] Toss expired medications (take to a pharmacy drop-box, not the trash or toilet)
- [ ] Toss expired cosmetics, old sunscreen, half-empty bottles
- [ ] Pack decorative items and extra towels in medium boxes
- [ ] Pack non-daily toiletries in a medium box, double-bag liquids in ziplocks
- [ ] Shower curtain and rings: fold into a labeled bag
- [ ] Label: **GUEST BATH — [contents] — B**

*Primary bath (Day -3):*
- [ ] Pack most toiletries, leaving out a 3-day kit per person
- [ ] Bag all liquids (shampoo, lotion) individually
- [ ] Pack cleaning supplies you'll keep (double-bag, upright, mark "LIQUIDS")
- [ ] Hair tools: wrap cord around tool, pack in medium box
- [ ] Reserve toilet paper, hand soap, towels for the first-night box
- [ ] Label: **PRIMARY BATH — [contents] — A/B**

**Boxes needed per bath:** 2 medium, 1 small
**Declutter targets:** All expired meds, cosmetics older than 1 year, hotel toiletries, worn towels (donate to animal shelter), empty bottles, duplicate products
**Fragile:** Perfume bottles, glass jars — bubble wrap, double-bag

---

### Week 1 (Days -7 to -1): Daily-use spaces

---

**KITCHEN** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 5–7 hrs across 3 sessions**

*Session 1 (Day -7): Pantry + non-daily items*
- [ ] Donate unopened non-perishables to a food bank
- [ ] Toss expired food, spices older than 2 years, stale items
- [ ] Pack spices in a small box together (double-bag to contain spills)
- [ ] Pack baking supplies, canned goods, dry goods in small boxes (heavy)
- [ ] Specialty appliances (stand mixer, bread maker, slow cooker): medium boxes with paper fill
- [ ] Small appliances you rarely use: medium boxes
- [ ] Serveware, platters, holiday dishes: dish pack

*Session 2 (Day -4): Non-daily dishware + cookware*
- [ ] Wrap each plate individually; pack vertically in dish pack
- [ ] Glasses and stemware: individual wrap, vertical, dish pack only
- [ ] Mugs: wrap, pack upright
- [ ] Pots and pans: nest with paper between, medium box
- [ ] Baking sheets, cutting boards: stand vertically in medium box
- [ ] Knives: wrap blade in cardboard, tape shut, label clearly
- [ ] Cookbooks: small boxes only (heavy)
- [ ] Mixing bowls, measuring cups: medium box
- [ ] Tupperware/food storage: medium box (nest pieces)

*Session 3 (Day -1): Daily use*
- [ ] Reserve for first-night box: 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 mugs, 4 sets of utensils, 1 pan, 1 pot, dish soap, sponge, paper towels, coffee/tea setup, can opener, chef's knife + cutting board
- [ ] Pack everything else remaining
- [ ] Defrost fridge/freezer 24 hrs before move; wipe dry; prop open
- [ ] Toss or give away remaining perishables
- [ ] Empty icemaker, disconnect water line if moving the fridge

**Boxes needed:** 6–8 small, 8–10 medium, 3–5 dish packs
**Fragile:** All glassware, ceramics, stoneware — dish packs only, vertical, "FRAGILE" on 3 sides
**Declutter targets:** Duplicate utensils, chipped dishes, single-use gadgets (quesadilla maker, avocado slicer), mismatched Tupperware and lids, expired pantry items, dead spices, worn-out pans, mugs you never use
**Label:** Daily-use kitchen = **A**; everything else = **B**

---

**LAUNDRY ROOM / UTILITY** — **Responsible: P** — **Time: 1–2 hrs** (Day -5)

- [ ] Finish all laundry 2 days before move
- [ ] Disconnect washer hoses day-of; drain and bag them
- [ ] Secure washer drum with transit bolts if you have them (check the manual)
- [ ] Unplug dryer; coil cord and tape to back
- [ ] Pack detergent, softener, cleaning supplies upright in a medium box, double-bagged, labeled **LIQUIDS**
- [ ] Iron, ironing board, drying rack: wrap and bundle
- [ ] Mop, broom, vacuum: bundle with stretch wrap
- [ ] Vacuum attachments and bags: small box
- [ ] Label: **LAUNDRY — [contents] — C**

**Boxes needed:** 1 small, 2 medium
**Declutter targets:** Old cleaning products you don't use, dried-out sponges, worn mops, laundry products you've replaced
**Note:** Movers won't take open bleach, ammonia, or flammable cleaners — see hazardous list below.

---

**PLANTS** — **Responsible: M** — **Time: 1–2 hrs** (Day -3 to Day 0)

Most interstate movers won't transport live plants. Options:
- [ ] Gift plants to friends, neighbors, or local nurseries
- [ ] Transport yourself in the car (water 2 days before; don't overwater)
- [ ] For car transport: use sturdy boxes with holes; wrap pots in plastic to catch soil; group by size
- [ ] Check Oregon's plant import rules — some states restrict agricultural plants and soil. Verify at Oregon Dept. of Agriculture before crossing the border.
- [ ] Keep plants out of direct sun in the car and away from the dog
- [ ] Water lightly on arrival; don't repot for 2 weeks

**Declutter targets:** Dying plants, duplicates, large plants that won't fit the new space

---

**VALUABLES** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 1 hr** (Day -2)

Never put these in the moving truck. They ride with you.
- [ ] Jewelry (zippered pouch, in a bag you carry)
- [ ] Watches, heirlooms, sentimental small items
- [ ] Cash, checkbooks, bonds, stock certificates
- [ ] Passports, birth certificates, Social Security cards, titles, wills
- [ ] Laptops, tablets, external hard drives, USB backups
- [ ] Prescription medications (keep in original bottles with labels)
- [ ] Firearms (if any — check interstate transport laws; store unloaded, locked, separate from ammo)
- [ ] Small collectibles of high value
- [ ] Photo albums, hard-to-replace sentimental items

**Container:** 1 locking box or carry-on suitcase; stays with you from loading day through arrival

---

**MISCELLANEOUS / CATCH-ALL** — **Responsible: J** — **Time: 2 hrs** (Day -2)

The stuff that doesn't belong to any room.
- [ ] Junk drawers: sort fast, toss duplicates, bag miscellany
- [ ] Batteries: collect in one bag; recycle dead ones
- [ ] Cables and cords (not already packed): bag and label by device
- [ ] Shoes by front door: pack in medium box
- [ ] Coat closet: wardrobe box or vacuum bags
- [ ] Umbrellas, hats, bags: medium box
- [ ] Mail pile: sort, shred, and clear before move day
- [ ] Key hook: collect all keys; label unknowns; dispose if unidentifiable
- [ ] Last-minute items on counters, in drawers: one labeled **MISC — LAST OUT** box

**Boxes needed:** 2–3 medium, 1 wardrobe box

---

## HAZARDOUS ITEMS — WHAT MOVERS WON'T TAKE

Movers legally cannot transport these. Use them up, give them away, or dispose properly. Don't leave them in the house or toss in regular trash.

**Flammables and combustibles:**
- Gasoline, kerosene, lighter fluid, propane tanks, charcoal
- Aerosol cans (spray paint, hair spray, cleaners)
- Matches, lighters, fireworks
- Nail polish and remover
- Paint (oil-based), paint thinner, turpentine, varnish

**Corrosives and poisons:**
- Bleach, ammonia, drain cleaner, oven cleaner
- Pool chemicals
- Pesticides, herbicides, fertilizers
- Car batteries, antifreeze, motor oil

**Explosives and pressurized:**
- Ammunition (transport yourself legally; check state rules)
- Scuba tanks, fire extinguishers, oxygen tanks
- Darkroom chemicals

**Perishables:**
- Open food, frozen food, refrigerated items
- Live plants (often)
- Produce

**Other:**
- Lithium batteries (loose); keep in devices
- Mercury thermometers

**Where to dispose:**
- **Household hazardous waste facility:** Most counties have free or low-cost drop-off days. Search "[your county] household hazardous waste" for Ohio.
- **Auto parts stores:** Take used motor oil, car batteries, antifreeze (AutoZone, Advance Auto, O'Reilly often accept for free)
- **Pharmacies:** Expired medications (CVS, Walgreens, and most police stations have drop-boxes)
- **Home improvement stores:** Many take old paint, batteries, CFL bulbs (Home Depot, Lowe's)
- **Propane tanks:** Exchange or return to a propane retailer
- **Fire extinguishers:** Fire department may accept
- **Ammunition:** Local shooting range, gun shop, or police non-emergency line

**Give-away options:**
- Open paint, cleaning supplies: offer to neighbors or Buy Nothing groups
- Unopened food: donate to a food bank
- Lawn chemicals: give to a neighbor

---

## FULL PACKING TIMELINE (10-Week Move)

A session = 2–3 hours. Mark each on the calendar.

### Weeks 10–8: Prep (no packing yet)

- [ ] **Week 10:** Order supplies, begin decluttering mentally, schedule donation pickups
- [ ] **Week 9:** Start declutter in garage and storage areas (don't pack yet; just sort keep/sell/donate/trash)
- [ ] **Week 8:** List items for sale online; schedule donation pickups for Week 5

### Week 7: Supplies + Declutter Finish

- [ ] **J — Day -49, Sat AM:** Pick up boxes, tape, markers, bubble wrap (1 hr)
- [ ] **J — Day -48, Sun:** Finish declutter sweep of all closets and storage (3 hrs)

### Week 6: Low-use spaces

- [ ] **J — Day -42, Sat AM:** Garage/basement — session 1 (3 hrs)
- [ ] **J — Day -41, Sun A

# Full 10-Week Packing Timeline (Continued)

A session = 2–3 hours unless noted. Days are relative to **MOVE DAY = Day 0**.

---

# Services & Subscriptions Timeline

**MOVE DAY = Day 0.** Negative days = before move. Positive days = after arrival.

---

## PRIORITY LEGEND

- **CRITICAL** — Life/safety/legal impact if missed (health insurance, prescriptions, car insurance)
- **HIGH** — Significant disruption or cost if missed (utilities, banking, mail)
- **MEDIUM** — Inconvenience, but recoverable (streaming, memberships)
- **LOW** — Nice to update when convenient (loyalty programs, catalogs)

---

## UTILITIES (OHIO SHUTOFF + OREGON START)

| Service | Ohio Action | Oregon Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electric | Final read, shutoff Day +1 | Start Day 0 or arrival day | Day -21 | Website or phone | J | HIGH | 20 min each |
| Natural gas | Final read, shutoff Day +1 | Start Day 0 or arrival day | Day -21 | Website or phone | J | HIGH | 20 min each |
| Water/sewer | Final read, shutoff Day +1 | Start Day 0 | Day -14 | Phone (often city/municipal) | J | HIGH | 15 min each |
| Trash/recycling | Cancel Day +1 | Start arrival week | Day -14 | Phone or website | M | MEDIUM | 15 min each |
| Internet | Cancel Day 0 (return equipment) | Install Day 0 or ASAP | Day -42 | Phone | J | CRITICAL | 30 min + install visit |
| Cable/TV | Cancel Day 0 | Decide if restarting | Day -14 | Phone (retention lines try to keep you) | P | MEDIUM | 30 min |
| Home phone (landline) | Cancel Day 0 | Decide if restarting | Day -14 | Phone | P | LOW | 15 min |
| Propane / oil (if any) | Final delivery stop | Set up if needed | Day -21 | Phone | M | MEDIUM | 15 min |
| Lawn/snow service | Cancel Day 0 | Set up after arrival | Day -14 | Phone or text | M | LOW | 10 min |
| Pest control | Cancel Day 0 | Set up after arrival | Day -14 | Phone | M | LOW | 10 min |
| HOA (if applicable) | Notify + final dues | Register with new HOA if any | Day -30 | Email | J | HIGH | 20 min |

**Tips:**
- Schedule Ohio shutoffs for the day **after** your move, in case of delays.
- Schedule Oregon starts for the **day of arrival** or one day prior.
- Return cable boxes, modems, and routers in person to avoid unreturned equipment fees. Get a receipt.
- Internet install is the #1 backlog item — book it at Week 6 minimum.

---

## FINANCIAL

| Service | Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary bank | Address change, notify of move | Day -14 | Website or app | J | CRITICAL | 15 min each account |
| Credit cards (each) | Address change | Day -14 | App or website | J | CRITICAL | 10 min each |
| Investment / brokerage | Address change | Day -14 | Website | J | HIGH | 15 min each |
| Retirement (401k, IRA) | Address change | Day -14 | Website or employer HR | J | HIGH | 15 min each |
| Student loans | Address change | Day -14 | Website | Individual | HIGH | 10 min |
| Mortgage lender (if any) | Payoff coordination or address change | Day -30 | Phone | J | CRITICAL | 30 min |
| Venmo, PayPal, Cash App | Address change | Day -7 | App | J | MEDIUM | 5 min each |
| IRS | Form 8822 (change of address) | Day -7 | Mail or next return | J | HIGH | 15 min |
| Ohio Dept. of Taxation | Notify of move date | Day +7 | Website | J | HIGH | 15 min |
| Oregon Dept. of Revenue | Register as new resident at tax time | Day +7 | Note for tax season | J | MEDIUM | — |
| Social Security Admin | Address change | Day -7 | ssa.gov account | Each person | HIGH | 10 min each |

**Bank tip:** Call your bank before the move and ask if they have Oregon branches or if they're online-only. Some regional banks may require you to switch.

---

## INSURANCE

| Service | Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto insurance | Switch to Oregon policy (rates + coverage differ by state) | Day -14, active Day 0 | Phone or agent | J | CRITICAL | 45 min |
| Health insurance | Confirm Oregon network; check if plan is portable | Day -30 | Phone | Each person | CRITICAL | 30 min each |
| Dental / vision | Confirm Oregon providers in-network | Day -14 | Website | Each | HIGH | 15 min each |
| Renters insurance | Cancel Ohio, start Oregon (effective Day 0) | Day -7 | Website | J | CRITICAL | 30 min |
| Homeowners insurance (if selling) | Cancel after closing | Day -7 | Phone | J | HIGH | 20 min |
| Life insurance | Address change | Day -7 | Phone or website | Each | MEDIUM | 10 min each |
| Pet insurance | Address change, update vet on file | Day -7 | Website | M | MEDIUM | 10 min |
| Umbrella policy (if any) | Address change | Day -7 | Agent | J | MEDIUM | 15 min |

**Health insurance tip:** If you're on an ACA marketplace plan, a move is a qualifying life event — you may need to re-enroll in Oregon through the state exchange within 60 days.

---

## MEDICAL

| Service | Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary care doctor | Request records; ask for referrals | Day -30 | Phone or portal | Each | CRITICAL | 30 min |
| Specialists | Request records | Day -30 | Portal | Each | HIGH | 20 min each |
| Dentist | Request records | Day -14 | Portal | Each | MEDIUM | 15 min |
| Vision / optometrist | Current prescription + records | Day -14 | Portal | Each | MEDIUM | 15 min |
| Pharmacy | Transfer prescriptions to Oregon location | Day -7 | Phone or app | Each | CRITICAL | 15 min each |
| Therapist / mental health | Confirm teletherapy coverage in Oregon OR transfer records | Day -30 | Phone | Each | CRITICAL | 30 min |
| Vet (dog) | Records, rabies cert, meds | Day -42 | In person | M | CRITICAL | 1 hr (visit) |

**Pharmacy tip:** CVS and Walgreens can transfer prescriptions between their own locations easily. For independents, your new pharmacy will usually call the old one if you give them the number.

## MAIL & ADDRESS

| Service | Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| USPS change of address | Submit online (effective Day 0) | Day -14 | usps.com (~$1.10 verification fee) | J | CRITICAL | 15 min |
| Package forwarding | Update Amazon, Chewy, meal kits | Day -7 | Each app | J | HIGH | 30 min total |
| Voter registration | Update after arrival | Day +14 | sos.oregon.gov | Each | HIGH | 10 min each |
| Driver's license | Oregon license after arrival | Day +7 | DMV in person | Each | CRITICAL | 1–2 hrs |
| Vehicle registration | Oregon registration after arrival | Day +14 | DMV | M | CRITICAL | 1–2 hrs |

**USPS tip:** Set the start date to Day 0 or Day -1 to catch mail in transit. Forwarding is good for 12 months; use that window to update every sender.

| Spotify, Apple Music | Address change (for tax/billing) | Day -7 | App | Each | LOW | 5 min |
| Amazon Prime | Change default address | Day -7 | App | J | HIGH | 5 min |
| Costco / Sam's Club | Address change; find new location | Day -7 | Website | J | MEDIUM | 10 min |
| Gym / fitness (Planet Fitness, Orangetheory, etc.) | Cancel or transfer | Day -14 | In person or website | Each | MEDIUM | 20 min each |
| Yoga / studio classes | Cancel; check Oregon studio | Day -14 | Email or app | Each | LOW | 10 min |
| Meal kit (HelloFresh, Blue Apron) | Pause or update address | Day -14 | App | J | MEDIUM | 10 min |
| Pet food delivery (Chewy, etc.) | Update address + vet | Day -7 | Website | M | HIGH | 10 min |
| Magazines / print subscriptions | Address change or cancel | Day -14 | Website | Each | LOW | 10 min each |
| Audible, Kindle Unlimited | Address change (billing) | Day -7 | Account settings | Each | LOW | 5 min |
| News subscriptions (NYT, WSJ) | Address change | Day -7 | Account | Each | LOW | 5 min |
| Dollar Shave Club, Harry's, etc. | Address change | Day -14 | Account | Each | MEDIUM | 5 min |
| Wine club, CSA, local delivery | Cancel; find Oregon equivalents | Day -14 | Website | J | LOW | 10 min each |
| Charitable auto-donations | Update address | Day -7 | Website | Each | LOW | 5 min |

## EMPLOYMENT & GOVERNMENT

| Service | Action | Lead Time | Method | Who | Priority | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 401(k) / benefits admin | Address change | Day -7 | Portal | Each | HIGH | 10 min |
